chunks: What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:
I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man performed tawaf without wudu (ablution). He said: If it was voluntary, then let him perform wudu (ablution) and pray.

key_terms.تَطَوُّعًا: as a voluntary act, not obligatory
key_terms.وَلْيُصَلِّ: and let him perform the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on someone who performs voluntary tawaf without wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about tawaf performed without wudu (ablution). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that if the tawaf was voluntary, the person should perform wudu (ablution) and then offer the prayer, indicating a practical ruling tied to ritual purity in worship.
